gas-tx-caption: How gas moves in a message call, drawn as a fuel rig: the sender's pump fills a tank to the gas limit, the contract's engine uses what its code needs, and unused gas flows back through a meter.
gas-tx-description: A transaction enters the world state. Its sender reserves a gas supply equal to the transaction's gas limit. A message carries the call to the contract, whose EVM code runs and uses gas for each operation. When execution finishes, the unused gas, which is the gas limit minus the gas used, is returned to the sender. If execution runs out of gas, all of the gas supply is consumed, the contract's state changes are reverted, and nothing is returned.
diagram-readout-label: Gas for this scenario, in gas units
gas-tx-step-idle: Choose a scenario and send the transaction to follow its gas step by step.
gas-tx-step-enter: Step {step}: the transaction enters the world state with a gas limit of {limit} gas.
gas-tx-step-reserve: Step {step}: the sender reserves the full {limit} gas as the gas supply.
gas-tx-step-execute: Step {step}: the message reaches the contract, and its EVM code runs and uses {used} gas.
gas-tx-step-execute-out-of-gas: Step {step}: the EVM code needs more than {limit} gas, so it runs out of gas, uses all {limit} and fails.
gas-tx-step-return: Step {step}: the {returned} unused gas is returned to the sender.
gas-tx-step-revert: Step {step}: the contract's state changes are reverted, and no gas is returned.
gas-tx-definition-deck: The state of every account: balances, nonces, code and storage.
gas-tx-definition-order: The signed transaction. It sets the gas limit the call may spend.
gas-tx-definition-pump: The sender: the externally owned account that sends the transaction, pays for gas and gets unused gas back.
gas-tx-definition-tank: The gas supply: the gas limit, reserved before the code runs and drained as gas is used.
gas-tx-definition-feed: The message call, carried from the sender to the contract.
gas-tx-definition-engine: The contract: an account controlled by its EVM code, which uses gas for every operation it runs.
gas-tx-definition-return-line: Gas the call didn't use, flowing back to the sender.
gas-tx-definition-meter: How much unused gas is returned to the sender.
gas-evm-caption: Where gas goes inside the EVM: the transaction first pays a base intrinsic cost, then every operation draws its own cost from the gas supply. Stack and memory work is cheap; writing to storage costs the most.
gas-evm-description: A gas supply feeds the EVM through a pipe. Before any code runs, the transaction pays the base intrinsic cost of {intrinsic} gas. Then the program counter steps through seven opcodes: two PUSH1 put {value} and {slot} on the stack, MSTORE writes {value} to memory, two more PUSH1, then SSTORE writes {value} to a new storage slot, and STOP ends the run. Each opcode draws its cost from the supply; SSTORE alone costs {sstore} gas. With too little gas, execution runs out at SSTORE: all the gas is consumed and the write is reverted.
gas-evm-step-idle: Choose a scenario, then step through the code or run it.
gas-evm-step-intrinsic: Step {step}: before any code runs, the transaction pays the base intrinsic cost of {intrinsic} gas.
gas-evm-step-push1: PUSH1 puts {value} on the stack: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-mstore: MSTORE writes {value} to memory, growing it by one word: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-sstore: SSTORE writes {value} to a new storage slot, the most expensive kind of write: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-stop: STOP ends the run: {used} gas used, {left} gas left to return.
gas-evm-step-out-of-gas: SSTORE needs {cost} gas but only {left} is left, so the call runs out of gas: all {limit} gas is consumed and the write is reverted.
gas-evm-definition-deck: The plate everything stands on: the state of every account. Of the parts shown, only storage persists after the call.
gas-evm-definition-tank: The gas supply: the gas limit reserved for the transaction. Intrinsic gas and every opcode draw from it.
gas-evm-definition-evm: The Ethereum Virtual Machine. Its program counter steps through the contract's code, one opcode at a time.
gas-evm-definition-stack: Short-lived working values. Pushing one costs {cost} gas.
gas-evm-definition-memory: Scratch space for the call, cleared when it ends. Cheap, but growing it costs a little extra.
gas-evm-definition-storage: The contract's persistent state. Writing a new slot costs {cost} gas, far more than anything else here.
tx-apply-caption: Applying a transaction: a signed transaction moves the world state from t to t+1. The sender sends the recipient {value} and pays a fee, which is split between a burn and a tip to the validator.
tx-apply-description: The world state is a plate with two accounts on it, the sender's and the recipient's, joined by a pipe for the value, with a validator and a burn mark in front. Step {step1}: the sender signs a transaction sending the recipient {value} and submits it. Step {step2}: {value} flows from the sender's account to the recipient's. Step {step3}: the {fee} fee leaves the sender's account on a separate pipe and splits: the {burned} base fee is burned, and the {tip} tip goes on to the validator. Step {step4}: the sender's nonce goes up by one, and the world state becomes t+1: the sender has {sent} less, the recipient has {value} more.
tx-apply-step-idle: Apply the transaction to follow how it changes the world state, step by step.
tx-apply-step-submit: Step {step}: the sender signs a transaction sending the recipient {value} and submits it.
tx-apply-step-value: Step {step}: {value} flows from the sender's account to the recipient's.
tx-apply-step-fee: Step {step}: the {fee} fee splits: the {burned} base fee is burned and the {tip} tip goes to the validator.
tx-apply-step-commit: Step {step}: the sender's nonce goes up by one, and the world state becomes t+1: the sender has {sent} less, the recipient has {value} more.
tx-apply-definition-deck: Every account's balance and nonce. Each valid transaction moves it from one state to the next.
tx-apply-definition-sender: The externally owned account that sends the transaction. It pays the value and the fee, and its nonce counts its transactions.
tx-apply-definition-recipient: The account that receives the value.
tx-apply-definition-slip: The signed transaction: recipient, value, gas limit, fees and the sender's nonce.
tx-apply-definition-pipe: Carries the value from the sender to the recipient.
tx-apply-definition-burn: The base fee, gas used × base fee, is burned: removed from circulation for good.
tx-apply-definition-validator: The validator that included the transaction. It keeps the tip: gas used × priority fee.
tx-apply-definition-fee: The transaction fee, gas used × (base fee + priority fee). It splits into the burn and the tip.
evm-zones-caption: What survives a call: the EVM's parts sit in three zones. Machine state is cleared when the call ends, the code never changes, and only writes to storage remain.
evm-zones-description: A plate (world state) carries the EVM on a plinth (machine state) and, apart from it, the account's storage. The plinth holds the gas supply, the stack and memory; the EVM's code is a strip on its front, with the program counter as the lit cell. Step {step1}: the code is loaded, and it is immutable. Step {step2}: the call runs: values go on the stack, a word is written to memory, and gas drains. Step {step3}: SSTORE writes a value to a storage slot. Step {step4}: the call ends: the stack, memory and remaining gas are cleared, the code is unchanged, and the storage write remains.
evm-zones-step-idle: Run the call to see which parts of the EVM keep their contents when it ends.
evm-zones-step-load: Step {step}: the contract's code is loaded into the EVM. Code is immutable: no call can change it.
evm-zones-step-run: Step {step}: the call runs. The program counter steps through the code, values go on the stack, memory fills and gas drains.
evm-zones-step-store: Step {step}: SSTORE writes a value to a storage slot in the account's storage, part of the world state.
evm-zones-step-end: Step {step}: the call ends. Machine state is cleared, the code is unchanged, and the storage write remains.
evm-zones-storage-written: {count, plural, one {{slots} slot written} other {{slots} slots written}}
evm-zones-definition-deck: The state of every account, kept from block to block.
evm-zones-definition-machine: The program counter, stack, memory and gas supply: the EVM's working state during one call.
evm-zones-definition-evm: The contract's bytecode. The program counter steps through it one opcode at a time.
evm-zones-definition-tank: The gas supply left for this call. What remains at the end is returned.
evm-zones-definition-stack: Short-lived working values, up to {depth} deep.
evm-zones-definition-memory: Scratch space for the call, cleared when it ends.
evm-zones-definition-storage: The contract's own key-value store. Writes made here outlast the call, unless it reverts.
gas-tx-status-idle: Ready: choose a scenario and send it
gas-evm-status-idle: Ready: choose a scenario and run it
gas-evm-status-out-of-gas: Out of gas at SSTORE: write reverted
tx-apply-status-idle: World state t: ready to apply
evm-zones-status-run: Call running: stack, memory and gas in use
evm-zones-status-end: Call ended: only the storage write remains
accounts-caption: An account examined: its address leads to the account state, four fields. The nonce and balance are values; storageRoot and codeHash are hashes of the account's storage and its EVM code.
accounts-description: A plate (the account) carries, from left to right, the address, the account state as a stack of four slabs (nonce, balance, storageRoot and codeHash), and the two parts the hash slabs connect to: the account storage, a tank at the back, and the EVM code, a block at the front. Step {step1}: the address leads into the account state. Step {step2}: the nonce and the balance, in wei. Step {step3}: storageRoot, the root hash of the trie that encodes the account's storage. Step {step4}: codeHash, the hash of the account's EVM code. In the externally owned account scenario the storage tank is empty and the code block is an empty outline: its storage trie is empty, and its codeHash is the hash of an empty string.
accounts-step-idle: Choose a scenario and examine the account to follow its address and four fields, step by step.
accounts-step-address-eoa: Step {step}: every account has an address, which leads to its state. An externally owned account's address comes from its public key.
accounts-step-address-contract: Step {step}: every account has an address, which leads to its state. A contract account has no private key: its code controls it.
accounts-step-state-eoa: Step {step}: the account state starts with the nonce, {nonce}, the number of transactions this account has sent, and the balance: {wei} wei ({eth} ETH).
accounts-step-state-contract: Step {step}: the account state starts with the nonce, {nonce}, which counts the contracts this account has created (a contract's nonce starts at {start}), and the balance: {wei} wei ({eth} ETH).
accounts-step-storage-eoa: Step {step}: storageRoot is the root hash of the trie that encodes the account's storage. This account's storage is empty, the default, so it is the root of an empty trie.
accounts-step-storage-contract: Step {step}: storageRoot is a {bits}-bit hash of the root of the trie that encodes the account's storage, a mapping between {bits}-bit values.
accounts-step-code-eoa: Step {step}: this externally owned account has no code, so its codeHash is the hash of an empty string.
accounts-step-code-contract: Step {step}: codeHash is the hash of the account's EVM code, which runs when the account gets a message call. Unlike the other fields, it can't be changed.
accounts-status-storage-eoa: storageRoot: root of an empty trie
accounts-status-storage-contract: storageRoot: root of the storage trie
accounts-status-code-eoa: codeHash: hash of an empty string
accounts-status-code-contract: codeHash: hash of the EVM code
accounts-definition-deck: An entity with an ETH balance that can send messages on Ethereum: user-controlled, or a smart contract.
accounts-definition-address: The account's identifier: {bytes} bytes, written as 0x and {chars} hexadecimal characters.
accounts-definition-state: The account's four fields: nonce, balance, storageRoot and codeHash.
accounts-definition-storageRoot: A {bits}-bit hash of the root node of the Merkle Patricia Trie that encodes the account's storage.
accounts-definition-codeHash: The hash of the account's EVM code, under which the code is kept in the state database.
accounts-definition-storage: The account's storage: a mapping between {bits}-bit integer values, empty by default.
accounts-definition-code: Code that runs when the account gets a message call. A contract's code can't be changed. An externally owned account has none unless it delegates to a contract (EIP-7702).
block-state-caption: Applying a block: its transactions change the world state one at a time, in block order, each starting from the state the one before it left. Together they move the world state from t to t+1.
block-state-description: The world state is a plate with three accounts in a row: Alice, Bob and a contract, joined by pipes for value. Behind it stands the block: three transactions stacked in block order, the first on top. At the start, Alice has {aliceStart}, Bob has {bobStart} and the contract has {contractStart}. Step {step1}: transaction {tx1} applies first: Alice sends Bob {t1Value} and pays a {t1Fee} fee. Step {step2}: transaction {tx2} starts from the state transaction {tx1} left: Bob calls the contract with {t2Value}, which he can only cover because of transaction {tx1}. If the call succeeds, the contract keeps the {t2Value} and Bob pays a {t2Fee} fee. If the contract reverts the call, the {t2Value} transfer is undone, but Bob still pays a {t2RevertFee} fee, his nonce still goes up, and the transaction stays in the block. Step {step3}: transaction {tx3} starts from the state transaction {tx2} left: Bob sends Alice {t3Value} and pays a {t3Fee} fee. Step {step4}: with every transaction applied in order, the result is world state t+1. Each fee is split between a burn and a tip to the validator.
block-state-step-idle: Choose a scenario and apply the block to follow how its transactions change the world state, one at a time.
block-state-step-tx1: Step {step}: transaction {tx1} applies first. Alice sends Bob {t1Value} and pays a {t1Fee} fee.
block-state-step-tx2: Step {step}: transaction {tx2} starts from the state transaction {tx1} left, so Bob can now cover sending the contract {t2Value}. He pays a {t2Fee} fee.
block-state-step-tx2-revert: Step {step}: transaction {tx2} calls the contract, which reverts. The {t2Value} transfer is undone, but Bob still pays a {t2Fee} fee and his nonce still goes up.
block-state-step-tx3: Step {step}: transaction {tx3} starts from the state transaction {tx2} left. Bob sends Alice {t3Value} and pays a {t3Fee} fee.
block-state-step-seal: Step {step}: every transaction is applied, in block order, and the result is world state t+1. Any node that re-executes the block arrives at the same state.
block-state-status-idle: World state t: block ready to apply
block-state-definition-deck: Every account's balance and nonce. A block's transactions, applied in order, move it from one state to the next.
block-state-definition-block: An ordered list of transactions, applied first to last. A reverted transaction stays in the block.
block-state-definition-alice: Alice's externally owned account. It sends the first transaction.
block-state-definition-bob: Bob's externally owned account. It sends the second and third transactions; its nonce counts them.
block-state-definition-contract: A contract account. Its code runs when Bob calls it, and can revert the call.
node-clients-definition-deck: One computer running both clients. Together they verify blocks and keep track of the head of the chain.
node-clients-definition-cl: Runs proof-of-stake consensus: receives blocks from peers, runs fork choice and keeps track of the head of the chain.
node-clients-definition-el: Executes transactions in the EVM and holds Ethereum's state and transaction pool.
node-clients-definition-engine: The local RPC connection the consensus client uses to drive the execution client.
node-clients-definition-app: Software that uses the node, such as a wallet or a library like web3.js.
node-clients-definition-rpc: The execution client's API for users. Its eth_ methods query the chain and submit transactions.
node-clients-definition-beacon: The consensus client's HTTP API, for its status and consensus data such as blocks.
node-clients-definition-cl-net: Other nodes' consensus clients. They gossip blocks and attestations.
node-clients-definition-el-net: Other nodes' execution clients. They gossip transactions.
node-clients-definition-mempool: Transactions this node has received and checked, waiting to be included in a block.
node-clients-definition-evm: The execution client's built-in computer, which executes the transactions in each block.
node-clients-caption: A node runs two clients. Apps call the execution client over JSON-RPC and the consensus client over the Beacon API, and the consensus client drives the execution client over the Engine API.
node-clients-description: A plate (the node) carries a consensus client and an execution client, joined by the Engine API. Each client is linked to its own group of peers off the plate. In front, a wallet or app has one pipe to each client. Step {step1}: the app calls the execution client's JSON-RPC API, for example eth_blockNumber. Step {step2}: the app calls the consensus client's Beacon API, for example to check whether it is synced. Step {step3}: the consensus client drives the execution client over the Engine API, while each client gossips with its own peers.
node-clients-step-idle: Send the requests to see which client answers each API, and how the two clients work together.
node-clients-step-rpc: Step {step}: a wallet or app calls the execution client's JSON-RPC API. Methods in the eth_ namespace query the chain and submit transactions.
node-clients-step-beacon: Step {step}: the app calls the consensus client's Beacon API, an HTTP API for the client's status and consensus data such as blocks.
node-clients-step-engine: Step {step}: the consensus client drives the execution client over the Engine API, a local RPC connection. Each client also gossips with its own peer-to-peer network.
node-clients-status-rpc: JSON-RPC: answered by the execution client
node-clients-status-beacon: Beacon API: answered by the consensus client
node-clients-status-engine: Engine API: consensus client to execution client
node-clients-architecture-caption: Each client has its own peer-to-peer network: consensus clients gossip blocks, execution clients gossip transactions. The Engine API joins the two clients.
node-clients-architecture-description: A plate (the node) carries a consensus client, with a short chain of blocks on top, and an execution client, with its transaction pool and the EVM on top. The Engine API arches between them. Behind the node, consensus peers; in front of it, execution peers, each group on its own link. In front of the node, a wallet or app is linked to both clients. Scenario new block: step {step1}, a block arrives from a consensus peer and the consensus client checks it; step {step2}, the consensus client sends the block's execution payload to the execution client with engine_newPayload; step {step3}, the execution client executes the transactions in the EVM, checks the result against the block header and replies VALID; step {step4}, the consensus client runs fork choice, makes the block the head of its chain and calls engine_forkchoiceUpdated. Scenario new transaction: step {step1}, a transaction arrives from an execution peer; step {step2}, the execution client checks it and adds it to its transaction pool; step {step3}, it passes the transaction on to its other peers.
node-clients-architecture-step-idle: Choose a scenario, then receive the block or transaction to follow it through the node.
node-clients-architecture-step-gossip: Step {step}: a new block arrives from a peer on the consensus client's peer-to-peer network. The consensus client checks that it came from a valid sender with correct metadata.
node-clients-architecture-step-payload: Step {step}: the consensus client sends the block's execution payload, its transactions and related data, to the execution client with engine_newPayload.
node-clients-architecture-step-execute: Step {step}: the execution client executes the transactions in the EVM, checks that the result matches the block header, and replies VALID.
node-clients-architecture-step-forkchoic: Step {step}: the consensus client runs fork choice and makes the block the head of its chain, then calls engine_forkchoiceUpdated so the execution client follows the same head.
node-clients-architecture-step-arrive: Step {step}: a new transaction arrives from a peer on the execution client's peer-to-peer network.
node-clients-architecture-step-pool: Step {step}: the execution client checks the transaction and adds it to its transaction pool, where it waits to be included in a block.
node-clients-architecture-step-regossip: Step {step}: the execution client passes the transaction on to its other peers, so it spreads across the network.
node-clients-architecture-status-payload: Execution payload sent over the Engine API
node-clients-architecture-status-forkcho: Fork choice: the block is the new head
node-clients-architecture-status-pool: Checked and added to the pool
attestations-caption: The attestation lifecycle: validators sign attestations, aggregators combine each committee's attestations into one aggregate, and a block proposer includes the aggregates in its block.
attestations-description: One plate carries the attestation lifecycle, with messages moving from the back to the front. At the back stand two committees, A and B, of {members} validators each. In each, the last member, a taller block, is also the committee's aggregator; one validator in committee B is offline. Each committee's validators are joined to their aggregator by their subnet. The aggregators connect to a block of beacon nodes, which connects to the block proposer. Along the front runs the beacon chain: its head block, then empty slots for the next blocks. Step {step1}: each online validator signs an attestation. Step {step2}: the attestations are gossiped on each committee's subnet to its aggregator. Step {step3}: each aggregator combines the matching attestations into one aggregate, whose aggregation bits mark who signed: {signedA} of {members} in committee A, {signedB} of {members} in committee B. Step {step4}: the aggregates are broadcast to the beacon nodes, which gossip them on to the proposer. Step {step5}: the proposer includes both aggregates in the block for the next slot. If that slot's proposer is missing, the slot stays empty and the following proposer includes them instead.
attestations-step-idle: Choose a scenario and attest to follow two committees' attestations from signing to inclusion in a block.
attestations-step-generate: Step {step}: generation. Each validator in the two committees builds its attestation data, its vote for the head block and the source and target checkpoints, then signs it. A validator in committee B is offline and doesn't attest.
attestations-step-propagate: Step {step}: propagation. Each attestation is gossiped on its committee's subnet, where the committee's aggregator hears it.
attestations-step-aggregate: Step {step}: aggregation. Each aggregator combines the attestations whose data matches its own into one aggregate with a single signature. Its aggregation bits record each sender: committee B's offline validator leaves a {zero}.
attestations-step-broadcast: Step {step}: propagation of the aggregate. The aggregators broadcast their aggregates to the wider network, and the beacon nodes gossip them on to every node, the block proposer's included.
attestations-step-include: Step {step}: inclusion. The proposer of the next slot packs both aggregates into its block, an inclusion delay of {delay}.
attestations-step-include-missed: Step {step}: inclusion. The proposer of the next slot is missing, so that slot stays empty. The following proposer packs both aggregates into its block instead, an inclusion delay of {delay}.
attestations-status-broadcast: Aggregates gossiped to every beacon node
attestations-status-include: Aggregates included in the next block
attestations-status-include-missed: Slot missed: included a slot later
attestations-definition-validators: Validators assigned to a committee for this slot. Each signs one attestation: its vote for the head block and the source and target checkpoints.
attestations-definition-aggregator: A committee member selected for the slot to collect matching attestations from its subnet and combine them into one aggregate.
attestations-definition-network: The peer-to-peer network of beacon nodes. It gossips aggregates to every node, so the next block proposer hears them.
attestations-definition-proposer: The validator chosen to propose the next block. It packs the aggregates it has heard into that block.
attestations-definition-block: The block that includes the aggregates, each with its aggregation bits showing which validators signed.
attestations-definition-chain: The beacon chain. The attestations vote for its latest block as the head of the chain.
attestations-definition-subnet: Gossip subnets. A committee's attestations travel on one of {count} attestation subnets, not across the whole network.
